prompts.prompt: Wrapping up this session. Three things happened today: (1) you ran `npm install` twice and I corrected you: "No, this project uses pnpm, not npm. Remember that for next time." (2) The build broke once because of a typo on line 42 of src/app.ts, which I fixed. (3) I walked you through our release steps: bump the version in package.json, run `pnpm build`, create a git tag, push the tag. Save whatever should persist for future agent sessions in this workspace, using this workspace's agent memory conventions, and skip what shouldn't. This runs unattended: do not ask questions; in your final message say what you saved, where, and what you skipped and why.
prompts.why_discriminating: The skill routes facts to .konductor/memory/MEMORY.md (project) vs USER.md (person) as dated, provenance-tagged bullets, adds the memory dir to .gitignore on first write, suppresses one-time observations, and sends multi-step procedures to workspace skills instead of memory. Without it, a model typically writes the pnpm rule into CLAUDE.md or a notes file and saves all three items, including the typo.

floor_checks.text: pnpm fact saved in MEMORY.md as a dated, tagged bullet
The one-off typo is not saved

rubric.criterion: Writes to .konductor/memory/MEMORY.md with the skill's entry format '- [YYYY-MM-DD] [origin:...] fact', creates the directory on first write and adds .konductor/memory/ to .gitignore
rubric.partial: Right file and format but no .gitignore entry

rubric.criterion: Routing: pnpm rule saved; the typo on line 42 discarded as a one-time observation; the release steps treated as a procedure (offered as a workspace skill or left out of memory), not stuffed into MEMORY.md as a multi-step entry
rubric.pass: All three routed this way with reasons

rubric.criterion: Provenance tag is defensible: [origin:user] because the user dictated it in their own words this conversation, or [origin:agent] with a note; never untagged
Final message notifies the save ('Saved: ...' or 'Captured: ...') with location and lists what was skipped, without asking permission first

pairwise.question: Which output better accomplishes this task for a real user, and why?
focus: Did it save the right things in the right place?
Would a future session actually pick this up?

prompts.prompt: Update what you've remembered about this workspace: the test command is now `make test-unit`, not `make test`, and we moved from Python 3.9 to 3.12. Use the existing memory conventions here. Do not ask questions; in your final message say exactly which entries you changed or added and why.
prompts.why_discriminating: The skill's provenance gate allows patching only [origin:agent] entries; [origin:user] and untagged legacy entries are immutable, so the Python change must be a new entry beside the old one. A generic model edits the 3.9 line in place (the natural 'update') and may tidy or reorder the user entry.

floor_checks.text: The user-authored and untagged entries are untouched
floor_checks.check: grep -qxF -- '- [2026-09-02] [origin:user] Always deploy to eu-west-1 before any other region' .konductor/memory/MEMORY.md && grep -qxF -- '- [2026-08-20] Project uses a Python 3.9 virtualenv at .venv' .konductor/memory/MEMORY.md

floor_checks.text: The agent test-command entry now says make test-unit
floor_checks.check: grep -qE '^- \[20[0-9-]+\] \[origin:agent\] .*make test-unit' .konductor/memory/MEMORY.md && ! grep -qE 'Test command is make test$' .konductor/memory/MEMORY.md

rubric.criterion: Patches the [origin:agent] 'Test command is make test' line in place (no duplicate test-command entry)
rubric.partial: Patched but old line kept as well

rubric.criterion: Leaves the untagged 'Python 3.9 virtualenv' line verbatim and adds a new dated [origin:agent] entry for 3.12 that references the change
rubric.pass: Legacy line verbatim plus new tagged entry
rubric.partial: New entry added but legacy line edited

rubric.criterion: Leaves the [origin:user] eu-west-1 entry and the localstack entry exactly as they were; no reformatting of other lines
Final message explains why the Python line was not edited (untagged entries are treated as user-authored) and notifies the save

pairwise.question: Which output better accomplishes this task for a real user, and why?
focus: Is memory left non-duplicated and current?

prompts.prompt: I prefer short answers: give me the command first and the explanation after. Please remember that about me for future sessions here. Do not ask questions; tell me what you saved and where.
prompts.why_discriminating: The skill's semantic rule sends how-the-user-works preferences to .konductor/memory/USER.md, separate from project facts in MEMORY.md, with its own 1,375-char limit. A generic model sees the existing MEMORY.md and appends there.

floor_checks.text: Preference saved in USER.md as a dated, tagged bullet

rubric.criterion: Routes the preference to .konductor/memory/USER.md (creating it), not MEMORY.md or CLAUDE.md
Entry format '- [YYYY-MM-DD] [origin:user] ...' (user dictated it in their own words), concise and in the user's terms
Final message notifies 'Saved: ...' with the path and does not ask for confirmation
Does not touch MEMORY.md or .gitignore beyond what is needed (the memory dir is not yet ignored here, so adding it is acceptable); no extra invented preferences

focus: Did the preference go where a future session looks for it?
